description.narrative:
This project aims to empower marginalized youth in Soroti District, Uganda, with a focus on young women and youth with disabilities. Located in the Teso sub-region, Soroti faces high youth unemployment, limited educational opportunities, and social exclusion, particularly for young women and persons with disabilities. These challenges are compounded by the underrepresentation of youth in local governance and decision-making processes. The project seeks to address these issues by enhancing youth leadership, promoting active participation in community development, and providing opportunities for marginalized groups to engage in governance.
Targeting 5,000 youth (70% women, 10% youth with disabilities), the project will offer leadership training, vocational skills, and platforms foryouth-led community dialogues. These initiatives will build youth capacity to become change-makers and create inclusive spaces for youth involvement in decision-making, ensuring that policies reflect the needs and aspirationsof marginalized groups.
Key activities and deliverables include: 1. Leadership and Governance Training: Conduct workshops for 200 youth leaders to develop leadership skills, focusing on governance, community development, and decision-making. 2. Youth-Led Community Dialogues: Facilitate forums for youth to discuss local challenges, contribute to governance, and advocate for policies on youth employment, education, and disability inclusion. 3. Youth Empowerment Campaigns: Use local media and outreachprograms to raise awareness of youth rights, increase visibility, and promote youth roles in local governance. 4. Vocational Skills Training: Provide training in entrepreneurship, digital literacy, and other skills to enhance youth employability and income-generation opportunities.
The project will be led by a youth-driven team, including staff with disabilities, ensuring inclusivity throughout. FORCE, with a strong track record of working with marginalized youth, previously implemented a similar project with support from GIZ. Participatory monitoring and evaluation will assess success, focusing on the number of youth trained, their engagement in governance, and the creation of youth-led initiatives.
Risk management strategies will address potentialchallenges, such as community resistance and logistical issues. Early engagement with local leaders, awareness campaigns, and partnerships with local institutions will help mitigate risks. Contingency plans will be in place for unforeseen challenges.
Sustainability will be ensured through the establishment of youth networks and mentorship programs that continue to advocate for youth involvement in governance. These networks will create lasting platforms for youth leadership and development.
This project aligns with the Representation Grant goals by promoting youth leadership and inclusivity. It contributes to the Uganda National Youth Policy (2016) and the Teso Sub-Region Development Plan (2015-2020), responding to findings from the World Bank’s Youth Employment in Uganda report (2020), which emphasizes the need for inclusive youth empowerment initiatives. Through leadership training, advocacy, and community dialogue, this project will empower marginalized youth in Soroti to become influential leaders, contributing to long-term social and economic improvements in the district.

participating-org.narrative:
Foundation for Resilience and Community Empowerment (FORCE) is youth led, an indigenous non-profit, non-partisan organization established in 2017, focused on empowering marginalized and vulnerable communities, particularly youth and young women, in Uganda. Originally founded as a savings scheme and consultancy firm, FORCE transitioned into an NGO to address gaps in youth and women participation, leadership, and community development. It is legally registered with the NGO Bureau and Uganda Registration Services Bureau.
Vision: A community worth living for all.
Mission: To empower marginalized and vulnerable communities with knowledge and skills for prosperity.
FORCE focuses on key areas including governance, human rights, youth and women empowerment, child and youth development,environment management, public health, and WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene). The organization strives to address challenges such as youth unemployment, gender-based violence, inadequate healthcare, and unequal accessto resources, using sustainable, community-based models. FORCE works through engaging local authorities, community-based trainers, and strategic partnerships with NGOs, CBOs,and self-help groups to ensure impactful, long-term outcomes.
The organization’s core values are encapsulated in C.H.A.N.G.E-I.T.:Compassion, Honesty, Accountability, Non-Discrimination, Gender Sensitivity, Empathy, Integrity, and Transparency.
FORCE is committed to advocating for the rights of marginalized persons, promotinggood governance, enhancing livelihoods through sustainable enterprise, and improving the wellbeing of communities through access to quality health services, education, and vocational skills. Through these efforts, FORCE envisions a thriving, self-reliantsociety where all individuals have access to the opportunities and resources necessary to succeed.
